sections.h2: Choosing a sale route when you need to move fast
sections.html:
Austin owners usually pick among a standard listing, a sale they manage themselves, and a direct cash purchase. A cash buyer will close on your chosen day and accepts the property as is. A listing depends on showings, an appraisal and whatever financing the next buyer arranges.

Austin is expensive. The middle owner-occupied home is valued at $555,300, and just 43.4 percent of households own where they live. Because renters are so common, many Austin houses have been rentals or could become one, which shapes what an investor will pay and how quickly a deal can move.

  • Standard listing: the choice for an updated house priced close to nearby sales, if you can spare weeks for showings and a buyer's lender.
  • Self-managed sale: you set the price, draft the contract and negotiate, with a title company still handling the closing.
  • Cash purchase: a fit for deferred maintenance, an inherited house, a tenant who is staying or a firm deadline.

Austin passed one million residents: the July 2025 estimate is 1,002,632, roughly 4.6 percent over the April 2020 baseline of 958,151. In 2010 the count was 790,390.

Around 78.8 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier, and the average commute takes 23.7 minutes.

Austin's lakes came from dams on the Colorado River built in 1940 and 1941, which formed Lake Austin and Lake Travis and stopped the floods that had struck as late as 1935. Buyers know where the water is. A house next to a creek or on a lake invites flood questions that a house on higher ground does not.

Additions draw scrutiny as well. Since the 1970s, neighborhood groups and environmental ordinances have protected creeks, lakes and wooded hills. If you added a room without a permit, or your lot touches a creek, a buyer's inspector will ask. Pull permit records and any flood paperwork together before you list.

Each license is personal to the person holding it. Operating licenses are non-transferable, so anyone buying your house who wants nightly guests has to start a new application.

The council made short-term rental a secondary use on residential property in every zoning district in February 2025, for license holders. October 2025 changes extended each license to two years and removed the occupancy certificate and proof of insurance for new applicants and renewals. A tenant may hold one with the landlord's permission.

  • On single-family sites one person can run two units, and any further units must sit 1,000 feet apart.
  • For multifamily sites the limit is whichever is larger, one unit or a tenth of the units.
  • The required local contact has to be in Travis, Williamson, Hays, Bastrop or Caldwell County and able to respond within two hours.
  • Neighbors within 100 feet get written notice of the contact when a license is issued or renewed.
  • Booking platforms must display license numbers and take down unlicensed listings on the city's request.

Land in the extraterritorial jurisdiction needs neither a city license nor local hotel tax, so look at the jurisdiction map on the city's short-term rental page before you tell a buyer what is permitted.

sections.h2: Homestead exemptions and the appraisal cap
sections.html:
An owner who lives in the house probably pays tax on less than the market value a buyer sees in the listing. School districts exempt $140,000 of a homestead, and its appraised value cannot rise more than 10 percent a year apart from new improvements.

The cap belongs to the owner who claimed the exemption, so an investor begins without it. Ask the title company to estimate the buyer's first full-year bill so the contract holds no surprise. Owners over 65, or with a disability, get an extra $60,000 school exemption and a school tax ceiling that can follow them to a replacement Texas homestead.

Exemptions are granted by Travis Central Appraisal District, while bills are collected by the Travis County tax office. The latter's tax breaks page links to each one, and the Comptroller's limitations page covers the cap and the ceiling.

Closing centers on the deed. The county clerk will not record it until a notary has acknowledged it or two witnesses have sworn to it.

  1. Locate your deed and tax statement, and ask lenders for payoff letters.
  2. Request payoffs for liens too. A tax lien attaches every January 1.
  3. Confirm which county records deeds for your parcel, since the city covers a lot of ground.
  4. Sign the settlement papers and the deed, then let the title company file it.

With an inherited house, title becomes the question: executor's deed, muniment of title order, or affidavit of heirship. The affidavit is only a sworn statement, and no law forces a third party to accept it, so find out early which document the title insurer will honor.

You can sell with back taxes owing, as long as they are paid first. Delinquency begins February 1, when a six percent penalty and one percent interest apply. Since the lien stays with the property, closing pays the balance from your proceeds.

Request a payoff figure from the Travis County tax office before you settle on a closing date. Any earlier year still open should be dealt with first, so the title company can issue a clean commitment. Keep the receipt.

sections.h2: Comparing offers on an Austin house
sections.html:
Look at the amount that reaches your account and the date it arrives. A higher price weighed down by repair credits, a slow financing window and a commission can net less than a lower cash bid with a firm date.

Press each buyer on tenants, unpermitted work and open code complaints, and find out whether the bid holds up through an inspection. Write down each deadline, then choose the offer that covers your payoff and matches your move. If two offers look close, the one with fewer conditions is usually the safer one to accept.

Ask for proof of funds from a cash buyer and a pre-approval letter from a financed one. Both are easy to produce for a serious buyer, and they tell you quickly which offers can actually close.

faqs.q: Can an Austin short-term rental license be handed to the new owner?
faqs.a: No, licenses stay with the holder. The buyer applies for a new one, and handing over your license history can smooth that application.
Yes, it is the county seat. Still, your tax bill names the county of record for your parcel, and that decides which clerk files the deed.

faqs.q: Does my homestead tax cap pass to the person who buys my Austin house?
faqs.a: No. Each owner's cap starts the January after that owner first qualifies, so a buyer who moves in and applies begins a fresh one. A buyer who rents the house out cannot claim it at all.

faqs.q: What if my Austin house has unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: It comes out of your proceeds at closing, as the lien follows the house. A bill left unpaid is delinquent from February 1 and picks up a six percent penalty and one percent interest.
About 1,002,632 people in 2025, 4.6 percent more than the 2020 base, spread over 319.94 square miles of land.
